scenes.visual: Title card 'How Fast a Level Follows' over the plasma tank. Reuses the first film's colour map. COLOUR MAP for both films: secretion (gland tap) ORANGE; hormone level (water line in the plasma tank) TEAL; clearance (drain: every way the body removes or breaks down the hormone) GREY; negative feedback = RED dashed arrow from the level back to the tap. Animals charcoal silhouettes, named on screen. All curves are computed from: change in level per minute = secretion per minute / V - k x level, k = ln 2 / half-life, equal effective volume V in every tank. Every number appears only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: Cortisol tells the liver to make more glucose. The adrenal releases it in pulses, roughly every sixty to ninety minutes. Does its level in the blood pulse too?
scenes.visual: Label 'adult human'. The ORANGE adrenal tap opens in short bursts on a time axis; a TEAL line beside it shows a question mark where its shape should be.
scenes.narration: Cortisol tells the liver to make more glucose. The adrenal releases it in pulses, roughly every sixty to ninety minutes. Does its level in the blood pulse too?

scenes.tts: The first film built a tank, with a gland's tap pouring in and a drain clearing out. The level settles where the two match. Now we time the drain.
scenes.visual: Brief replay of the first film's tank: ORANGE tap, TEAL line, GREY drain, RED dashed feedback arrow, which fades to the background. A stopwatch icon appears on the GREY drain.
scenes.narration: The first film built a tank, with a gland's tap pouring in and a drain clearing out. The level settles where the two match. Now we time the drain.

scenes.tts: Shut the tap. The level falls, but not in a straight line. The drain removes a constant fraction each minute. So the level halves, then halves again, in equal steps of time. Wherever it starts, each halving takes the same time.
scenes.visual: The tap closes. A computed TEAL decay curve draws on a time axis. Under it, equal-width GREY bars each labelled 'one half-life'. On-screen level marks: '1', '1/2', '1/4', '1/8'. A dashed straight line labelled 'not this' fades out.
scenes.narration: Shut the tap. The level falls, but not in a straight line. The drain removes a constant fraction each minute. So the level halves, then halves again, in equal steps of time. Wherever it starts, each halving takes the same time.

scenes.tts: The time for one halving is the hormone's half-life. In this example, a small peptide hormone has a half-life of five minutes. For cortisol, textbooks give about sixty to ninety minutes.
scenes.visual: Two labels slide in under the axis: 'illustrative peptide: half-life 5 min' and 'cortisol: about 60 to 90 min'. The peptide's curve plunges; cortisol's sags slowly.
scenes.narration: The time for one halving is the hormone's half-life. In this example, a small peptide hormone has a half-life of five minutes. For cortisol, textbooks give about sixty to ninety minutes.

scenes.tts: Now open the tap again and leave it open. The level climbs toward a new steady value, where the drain matches the tap. It gets halfway there in one half-life. It is nearly there after about four.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE tap reopens. A computed TEAL rising curve approaches a dashed line labelled 'new steady level'. Markers: '50% at 1 half-life', '75% at 2', '94% at 4'.
scenes.narration: Now open the tap again and leave it open. The level climbs toward a new steady value, where the drain matches the tap. It gets halfway there in one half-life. It is nearly there after about four.

scenes.tts: So the half-life sets the speed in both directions. A slow drain means a slow fall, and also a slow rise. The level always lags behind the tap. A short half-life lets a level answer its gland within minutes. A long one takes hours.
scenes.visual: The fall curve and the rise curve sit mirrored on one axis, both TEAL, each tick one half-life wide. A label 'same clock both ways'.
scenes.narration: So the half-life sets the speed in both directions. A slow drain means a slow fall, and also a slow rise. The level always lags behind the tap. A short half-life lets a level answer its gland within minutes. A long one takes hours.

scenes.tts: Now give two hormones the same tap. It opens in equal short bursts, like cortisol's pulses. One hormone has a fast drain. The other has cortisol's slow drain.
scenes.visual: Two tanks of equal volume side by side, one ORANGE tap feeding both in identical short bursts (bursts drawn as ORANGE blocks on a shared time axis, labelled 'one equal burst every 60 min, illustrative'). Left tank's GREY drain is wide, label 'half-life 5 min'; right tank's drain is narrow, label 'half-life 75 min'.
scenes.narration: Now give two hormones the same tap. It opens in equal short bursts, like cortisol's pulses. One hormone has a fast drain. The other has cortisol's slow drain.

scenes.tts: Same bursts, two drains. Before they run, make your call. Compared with its own average, which level will swing more with each burst?
scenes.visual: Both TEAL lines hidden behind a question card: 'Relative to its own average, which level swings more: fast drain or slow drain?'
scenes.narration: Same bursts, two drains. Before they run, make your call. Compared with its own average, which level will swing more with each burst?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Each burst adds the same amount to both tanks. The fast-draining level then empties before the next burst. So each burst lifts it far above its tiny average. The slow-draining level never empties. It ripples gently around a much higher middle.
scenes.visual: Computed traces at periodic steady state, both on the same vertical scale, same bursts (one equal instant burst every 60 min). Each burst adds the same jump to both levels; on screen 'same jump per burst in both tanks'. Left TEAL trace spikes and falls to near zero between bursts; on screen 'peak/trough = 2^(60/5), about 4,000-fold'. Right TEAL trace sits much higher with a gentle ripple; on screen 'peak/trough = 2^(60/75), about 1.7-fold'. Label 'computed, illustrative numbers; swings compared relative to each level'.
scenes.narration: Each burst adds the same amount to both tanks. The fast-draining level then empties before the next burst. So each burst lifts it far above its tiny average. The slow-draining level never empties. It ripples gently around a much higher middle.

scenes.tts: So with brief bursts, what matters is the half-life compared with the gap between them. Much shorter, and the level tracks each pulse. As long as the gap, and the level smooths them. In this model, cortisol's level still ripples with each pulse, but it never empties.
scenes.visual: The two traces shrink side by side, labelled 'brief pulses, model: tracks them when half-life is much shorter than the gap' (left) and 'smooths pulses: half-life about as long as the gap' (right). The right one is tagged 'cortisol-like'.
scenes.narration: So with brief bursts, what matters is the half-life compared with the gap between them. Much shorter, and the level tracks each pulse. As long as the gap, and the level smooths them. In this model, cortisol's level still ripples with each pulse, but it never empties.

scenes.tts: One rule still holds over many bursts. On average, the drain removes what the tap adds. A slow drain removes a smaller fraction each minute. So it needs a fuller tank to keep up. That is why the slow-draining level sits higher.
scenes.visual: A dashed TEAL line labelled 'average' appears through each trace, on the same vertical scale. Computed: 'average level = average secretion / (k x V)'. Right average labelled '75 / 5 = 15 times higher, same bursts'. Under the right trace: 'smaller swings relative to its average'.
scenes.narration: One rule still holds over many bursts. On average, the drain removes what the tap adds. A slow drain removes a smaller fraction each minute. So it needs a fuller tank to keep up. That is why the slow-draining level sits higher.

scenes.tts: These curves come from a simple model with invented numbers. Real secretion varies over time. It is rarely one steady rate, or switched off outright.
scenes.visual: A 'model' stamp over the curves. Beside them, an irregular ORANGE secretion trace labelled 'real secretion varies (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: These curves come from a simple model with invented numbers. Real secretion varies over time. It is rarely one steady rate, or switched off outright.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex. Take-home line: 'The half-life sets how fast a hormone level can follow.'
